_note: Mission notes filed from control, over the thirteen days of the run. kind is LOG, ANOMALY or BROADCAST; the science officer's daily findings (SCIENCE) and the health officer's daily activities (HEALTH) are written from the composers in mission control and land here too, one per day and kind. These appear on the landing page's whole-mission fold and in the archive. This is the file to add to during the run when something happens that is not in the schedule.

1.body: Hatch sealed at 06:45, Thursday 15 October. Pressure held two hours at nominal. The mission clock is running: thirteen days to Tuesday 27 October.

3.body: Condensation forming on the west wall overnight. Wipe-down added to the daily routine.

5.body: Water recovery loop running 4% below spec since 02:00. Cause not identified. Water allowance reduced at lunch.
Primary intake filter changed three days ahead of schedule. Dust load higher than modelled.

6.body: Exterior dust survey: deposition on the west panel costing 11% of generation. Panel cleaned at 11:00; generation recovered to within 3% of day one by evening.

7.body: Full inventory audit completed by hand at the midpoint. Logged figures confirmed; the water log was two litres optimistic. First shoots on trays 1 and 3.
Day seven of thirteen. Six days done, six to go. Earth is 226 million kilometres away tonight and every message takes twelve and a half minutes to arrive.

8.body: CO₂ rising faster than modelled during the sleep period. Scrubber cartridge swapped at 09:00. Levels nominal by 11:00. Spares now cycling at twice the planned rate.
West panel seal failed a second time. Repair deferred to day 10. One medical kit opened.

9.body: Water recovery membrane replaced. Loop revalidated to spec at 11:00. Full allowance restored from lunch. Last regolith collection: batch C, twelve samples.

10.body: First greenhouse harvest: 22 grams. Grown inside the habitat, from carbon the crew exhaled.
West panel seal, third attempt, left to cure overnight. Clocks go back one hour at 03:00 tonight: day 11 runs twenty-five hours, and the mission clock follows the venue.

11.body: Consumables projection to hatch open: 120 litres of water left at the current draw, oxygen reserve above 45%, scrubber spares sufficient. Seal holding. Second set of full crew readings taken.

12.body: Samples packed: three batches, thirty-six vials, boxed and labelled. Every log and reading copied to the carry-out drive.

13.body: Final count by hand: 84 litres of water, one day of food, oxygen reserve 48%, four scrubber cartridges, 26 kWh in the battery.
Hatch unseal at 21:00, Tuesday 27 October. The mission clock stops. The archive stays open.
